lines.japanese: 次の日も、俺は駅前のスチールパイプに腰かけていた。
lines.english: The next night, I was back on the steel railing outside the station.

lines.japanese: なんとなく目に入るマルチネスの露店は、そろそろ閉店準備に取りかかろうとしている。
lines.english: Martinez's stall sat in my line of sight, just getting ready to close for the night.

lines.japanese: １１月２２日の２２時。ゾロ目が揃って縁起良さげな祝日前夜。いや、カレンダーなんて俺には関係ない話だけどさ。
lines.english: Ten p.m. on November twenty-second. Matching digits everywhere, and the night before a holiday. Auspicious enough, I guess. Not that the calendar had much to do with me.

lines.japanese: さて今日は……どうっすかな……。
lines.english: So... what to do tonight...

lines.japanese: 財布を開けて野口の人数を確認すると（福沢は数えるまでもない）すぐに閉じた。昨日のぬるい稼ぎでは、豪勢なディナーと洒落こむわけにもいかない。
lines.english: I opened my wallet, counted the thousand-yen Noguchis inside—no Fukuzawas to bother counting—and snapped it shut. Yesterday's meager haul wasn't taking me anywhere fancy for dinner.

lines.japanese: とは言え、ただ貧困に憂えていても仕方ない。俺は職を求めてケツを上げた。よっこいしょ。
lines.english: Still, brooding over poverty would accomplish nothing. I got off my ass in search of work. Heave-ho.

lines.japanese: ヒゲ監督からまた来ていいと言われたのは幸いだったけど、その前に一応パルさんのところへも寄っておこう。独りでできる美味しい仕事が舞いこんでいればモアベターだ。
lines.english: Good thing Beard Boss had said I could come back. First, though, I ought to stop by Paru's and check in. If some cushy one-man job had landed in her lap, that'd be *more better*.

lines.japanese: 作業着その他の詰まったスポーツバッグを担ぎ、真冬の乾いたコンクリート舗装を踏みしめる。
lines.english: I shouldered the sports bag stuffed with my work clothes and assorted gear, then set off across the dry concrete of midwinter.

lines.japanese: 地下鉄入り口の脇で、ヒッピー風の貧乏くさい二人組がヘタウマのしゃがれ声を吐きながらアコースティックギターをかき鳴らしていた。
lines.english: Beside the subway entrance, a shabby pair of would-be hippies thrashed at acoustic guitars, their hoarse voices rough enough to circle back around to charming.

lines.japanese: 未来ある若者が、夢を目指して愛を謳う。結構なことじゃないか。
lines.english: Young people with futures ahead of them, chasing their dreams and singing of love. Couldn't argue with that.

lines.japanese: 安っぽい青春応援ロックを微笑ましい気分で聴きながら、俺は信号機よりもアルバトロスよりも高い紫色の空を眺める。
lines.english: I listened fondly to their bargain-bin youth anthem and looked up at a purple sky higher than a traffic light, higher even than an albatross.

lines.japanese: そういえば、今夜はアフリカ太鼓が聞こえない。
lines.english: Come to think of it, there were no African drums tonight.

lines.japanese: ピンクはメルヘン。ピンクはポルノ。そう考えると両者は意外と相性がいいのかもしれない。
lines.english: Pink was fairy tales. Pink was porn. Put that way, maybe the two were more compatible than you'd think.

lines.japanese: 歓楽街のいかがわしい風景にあっさり溶けこんだ、全面どピンクのファンシーなミニバン。
lines.english: A fanciful minivan painted violently pink from end to end, blending effortlessly into the sleaze of the entertainment district.

lines.japanese: それはある女の夢の形。その女は、いまは亡き母が初めて枕元でヘンゼルとグレーテルを読んでくれたころから西洋菓子屋に憧れてたっていう。
lines.english: It was one woman's dream given shape. She said she'd wanted a pastry shop of her own ever since her late mother first read *Hansel and Gretel* at her bedside.

lines.japanese: あたしゃクレープに幸せを包んで売ってるんだよ。あるとき女は、気分よく酔った拍子にそう言った。
lines.english: *Me, I wrap happiness in my crêpes and sell it.* She'd told me that once when she was pleasantly drunk.

lines.japanese: コイン一枚で買える幸せ。そのぐらいだったら俺の手に届かないこともない。
lines.english: Happiness you could buy with a single coin. Even I could reach that far.

lines.japanese: ポータブル発電機をがたがた震わせて、パル姐さんのお菓子の家はいつもの場所で営業していた。ＢＧＭは今日も今日とて、あの羽根付き扇子を振りまわしたくなる懐かしのテクノ。
lines.english: The portable generator rattled away as Paru's gingerbread house did business in its usual spot. Tonight's background music was, as ever, nostalgic techno that made you want to wave a feathered fan in the air.

lines.japanese: 先客がいる。カウンターの前でくっちゃべってる制服の女が三人。派手な笑い声。
lines.english: There were customers ahead of me: three girls in school uniforms chattering at the counter. Loud laughter.

lines.japanese: 夜遊びに相応しく制服を着崩した女たちを見る。濃紺のブレザーはきのう見た誰かのと似てたけど、スカートの色がまったく違っていた。
lines.english: I looked over the girls, their uniforms loosened into the proper attire for a night out. Their navy blazers resembled one I'd seen on somebody yesterday, though their skirts were a completely different color.

lines.japanese: ま、べつにどうでもいいんだけどな。
lines.english: Not that it mattered.

lines.japanese: 「ありあとぁしたー！」
lines.english: “Thaaank you!”

lines.japanese: 甘ったるい商品を受けとったそいつらと入れかわりに、ずんずんミニバンへ近付いていく。
lines.english: As they departed with their sugary purchases, I strode up to the minivan.

lines.japanese: 近付けば見えなかったものまで見えてくるのが世のことわり。バックドアのななめ後ろ、若い男女がふたりでひとつのクレープを分けあっていた。
lines.english: The closer you get, the more you see: such is the order of nature. Just behind the rear hatch, a young man and woman were sharing a single crêpe.

lines.japanese: でっかいイチゴが道路に落ちたって知らんぷりのくせに、彼氏の顎に付いたストロベリーソースはハンカチでそっと拭ってあげる心優しい彼女。
lines.english: The tenderhearted girlfriend ignored the enormous strawberry that fell into the street, but gently wiped the strawberry sauce from her boyfriend's chin with a handkerchief.

lines.japanese: 視線。はにかみ。忍び笑い。ふたりのために世界はあるの。ぇえぷ──失礼、げっぷ出ちゃったよ。
lines.english: Glances. Blushes. Secret little laughs. The whole world was made for us twooo—urrp. Excuse me. Burped.

lines.japanese: 「うす」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 俺はカウンターへ片肘を置き、車体で視界が狭まるように前のめりになった。鉄板を拭き掃除していたクレープ屋が、肩越しに振りかえってにやりと笑った。
lines.english: I planted one elbow on the counter and leaned forward until the van blocked my view. The crêpe seller looked back over her shoulder from wiping the griddle and grinned.

lines.japanese: 「おう、来たね芸人」
lines.english: “Well, look who's here. The comedian.”

lines.japanese: 「っせえな、女優に向かって芸人とか言うな」
lines.english: “Shut up. Don't call an actress a comedian.”

lines.japanese: 「で。調子はどうよ」
lines.english: “So? How's business?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、ぼちぼちかねえ」
lines.english: “Oh, can't complain.”

lines.japanese: パル姐さんはひねりのない答えをよこした。にたりと歯列を覗かせる気味の悪い笑顔。
lines.english: Paru gave me the stock answer with a creepy grin that showed every tooth.

lines.japanese: 「鳴坊なら日暮れの時分に来たよ」
lines.english: “Little Naru came by around sundown.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 鳴……あいつ、昨日の今日でさっそく来たのか。つーか、いきなりそんな報告されても。
lines.english: Naru... She’d actually come back the very next day? And what was I supposed to do with that information, dropped on me out of nowhere?

lines.japanese: 「ああそう」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah?”

lines.japanese: 俺は目を落とし、ラップ越しの商品見本を指で弾いた。ロウ細工の安っぽいイミテーション。
lines.english: I lowered my eyes and flicked a finger against the plastic-wrapped display sample. A cheap wax imitation.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、良かったじゃん。常連客一匹増えて」
lines.english: “Good for you, then. Got yourself one more regular.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえさん、あれだねえ。随分とまあ、あの子に懐かれたみたいじゃないかィ」
lines.english: “You know, that girl has certainly taken a shine to you.”

lines.japanese: 「なにそれ」
lines.english: “What's that supposed to mean?”

lines.japanese: 「だってあの子ったらよ、勿体つけてちみちみ食いながら、きょろッきょろ、きょろッきょろしてやんの。かーわいい、誰かさんを待ってたんじゃないかねえ、ありゃ」
lines.english: “Why, she took forever over that thing, nibbling away while her eyes went here, there, here, there. Cute as hell. Looked to me like she was waiting for somebody.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　べつに、元からそーゆー挙動不審な動きしてたじゃん、あいつ」
lines.english: “Huh? She’s always been twitchy like that.”

lines.japanese: 「それと、話してて思ったんだけどさ。あの子、いいとこの嬢ちゃんなんじゃないか？」
lines.english: “And something else struck me while we were talking. That girl's from money, isn't she?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ。ま、知らねーけどそうかもな」
lines.english: “Beats me. Could be.”

lines.japanese: 「門限とかも厳しいんじゃないかねえ。あんたさ、もっと早い時間に来たげなさいよ」
lines.english: “Strict curfew, too, I'll bet. You oughta start coming earlier for her.”

lines.japanese: 「知るかっつの。なんで俺がアレに合わせなきゃなんねーんだよ」
lines.english: “How the hell should I know? Why should I arrange my life around her?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでも何もあるかい、ドラだってゆうべは楽しそうだったじゃねえか。きひひ、参ったねどうも」
lines.english: “What do you mean, why? You had yourself a grand old time last night too, Dra. Kihihi. Lord, you two are a case.”

lines.japanese: 「っせえな……んなことよりさ、あんさ、なんか仕事入ってないの俺に」
lines.english: “Shut up... More importantly, you got any work for me?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうだ、来てる来てる。一件はエージので──」
lines.english: “Oh, right. I do, I do. One job's from Eiji—”

lines.japanese: 「エージからの仕事は無条件にキャンセルします」
lines.english: “Anything from Eiji gets an automatic no.”

lines.japanese: 「──もう一件は、登紀子さん」
lines.english: “—and the other is from Tokiko.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、登紀子さん……」
lines.english: “Ah. Tokiko...”

lines.japanese: 俺は模造品のクレープの輪郭を、二本の指でつつつとなぞった。毒々しい赤すぎるイチゴ。
lines.english: I traced the edge of the fake crêpe with two fingers. Its strawberry was a lurid, poisonous red.

lines.japanese: 登紀子さん、ていうのはたぶん源氏名。戸籍上の名前は知らない。俺とは親子ほどの差があるけど、不自然なほど生活臭がなくて、まあ歳のわりには美人だ。
lines.english: Tokiko was probably a name she used for work; I didn’t know her legal one. She was old enough to be my mother, but almost unnaturally free of any suggestion of domestic life. And, well, she was pretty for her age.

lines.japanese: 詳しいことは聞かされてないけど、身に付けてるものを見るまでもなく、明らかに金には困ってない感じ。
lines.english: No one had told me much about her, but you didn’t need to see how she dressed to know she wasn’t hurting for money.

lines.japanese: 会話の中でたまに「うちの店」とか「うちの若い子」なんて言葉を出してくるから、きっとどこか酒の飲める店の経営者なんだろう。柳木原ではそんな店が夜毎たくさん生まれたり死んだりしている。
lines.english: Now and then she’d mention “my place” or “one of my younger girls,” so I figured she ran some sort of bar or club. Places like that were born and died every night in Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: 「で。今回の依頼内容は」
lines.english: “So. What's the job this time?”

lines.japanese: 「下の子のクリスマスプレゼント買いに行くから、荷物持ちしてほしいってよ」
lines.english: “She's buying her younger child a Christmas present and wants you to carry the bags.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そう」
lines.english: “Ah. Right.”

lines.japanese: 登紀子さんの依頼はいつもそんな感じだ。楽っちゃ楽なんだけど、疲れるっちゃ疲れる──いや、疲れるの方が大きいか。
lines.english: Tokiko’s requests were always like that. Easy in one sense, tiring in another—no, mostly just tiring.

lines.japanese: 駅前で待ちあわせて、並んでデパートまで歩く。買い物が終われば、メニューに値段の書いてないフランス料理屋で肩のこる夕餉。２０歳ぐらい若返ったようなトーンで喋る登紀子さんに、俺は適当な相槌を打つ。
lines.english: We'd meet outside the station and walk side by side to the department store. Once the shopping was done, there'd be a stuffy dinner at a French restaurant with no prices on the menu. Tokiko would talk in a voice twenty years younger, and I'd just nod along.

lines.japanese: 夜が更ければ手を握られることもあったし、腕を取られたこともあったし、まあ、他にもちょっとゴニョゴニョだ。
lines.english: Once it got late, sometimes she’d take my hand, sometimes my arm, and, well... there’d been a few other things best left mumbled.

lines.japanese: 「登紀子さん、相ッ変わらず素人専門だねえ」
lines.english: “Tokiko still has a thing for amateurs, I see.”

lines.japanese: パルさんのその言葉は冗談でも冷やかしでもなく、本人が公言している事実だ。そうじゃなかったら柳木原には、俺より顔が良くて気が利いてベシャリも上手いプロのおにいさんがいくらでもいる。
lines.english: Paru wasn’t joking or teasing me. It was a fact Tokiko freely admitted. Otherwise, Yanagihara was full of professionals better-looking than me, more attentive, and a whole lot smoother with their patter.

lines.japanese: そんな登紀子さんの口癖は「私も人並の青春を過ごしてみたかったわぁ」だ。ひょっとしたら俺は、青い春を売っているのかもしれない。
lines.english: Tokiko’s favorite refrain was, “I wish I’d gotten to have an ordinary youth, too.” Maybe what I was selling her was the youth she’d missed.

lines.japanese: もっとも俺は、その青春ってやつが何物なのか、いまいち分かっていないんだけど。
lines.english: Not that I’d ever quite figured out what this thing called youth was supposed to be.

lines.japanese: 「あー、どうすっかなあ……」
lines.english: “Hmm. What should I do...”

lines.japanese: 「なんだい、どうするって。いつも即決なのに、なに今日は迷ってんだい」
lines.english: “What do you mean, what should you do? You always decide on the spot. What's got you wavering today?”

lines.japanese: 「迷ってるっつーかさあ……」
lines.english: “I wouldn't call it wavering...”

lines.japanese: ううむと腕を組んで背中を反らしたら、またあの馬鹿ップルが俺の視界に割りこんできた。
lines.english: I folded my arms with a groan and leaned back, and that idiotic couple came barging into view again.

lines.japanese: 男が女の口にクレープを運ぶ。あーん。女は一口かぶりついたあと、リップの上に残った精液みたいなバニラホイップを、わずかに覗かせた舌先ですくいとった。
lines.english: The guy held the crêpe to the girl’s mouth. Open wide. After one bite, she slipped out the tip of her tongue and licked the vanilla cream from her glossy lips, white as a smear of cum.

lines.japanese: 「要するに迷ってんだろ。どうすんだい」
lines.english: “That's what wavering means. So what's it going to be?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、なんだ……なんだコレ。なんか上がんねーんだよなあ、気分的に」
lines.english: “I dunno. What is this? My heart's just not in it today.”

lines.japanese: 俺はうしろ頭をがしがしと掻いた。
lines.english: I raked hard at the back of my head.

lines.japanese: 「んん？　なんだい、純潔を守りたくなるようなイイヒトでも現れたかい」
lines.english: “Hmm? Has some special someone appeared who makes you want to preserve your purity?”

lines.japanese: 「なわきゃねーだろ。いまさら俺に、そんなんあるかっつの。なんとなくだ、なんとなく」
lines.english: “Like hell. You think I've got any purity left to preserve at this point? It's nothing. Just a feeling.”

lines.japanese: 「なんとなくねぇ……」
lines.english: “Just a feeling, hmm...”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、それに登紀子さん、最近なんか旦那と上手くいってるみてーなこと言ってたしなあ。やだろ、だって、ある日ヤクザみたいのが青筋立てて怒鳴りこんできたら」
lines.english: “Besides, Tokiko said things have been going pretty well with her husband lately. You wouldn't like it either if some gangster-looking bastard came storming in one day with a vein popping out of his forehead.”

lines.japanese: 「でもあんた、この前までそんなの知ったこっちゃねぇって、目ぇ￥マークにして息巻いてたじゃないかぃ」
lines.english: “But up until the other day, you were all fired up, saying you didn't give a damn, with yen signs in your eyes.”

lines.japanese: 「んなもんシャレに決まってんだろ。ま、いいや。パルさん悪い、やっぱそれ断っといて」
lines.english: “That was obviously a joke. Whatever. Sorry, Paru, but tell her I'm passing after all.”

lines.japanese: 「へぃへぃ」
lines.english: “Aye, aye.”

lines.japanese: クレープ屋はなぜか片目を細めてにたにた笑った。
lines.english: For some reason, the crêpe seller narrowed one eye and kept grinning.

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ。へぃは一回でいんだよ。ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “What? One aye is enough. I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: しかし女はニタニタをやめなかった。俺はもう一回言った。
lines.english: But the woman kept grinning. I said it again.

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ。へぃは一回でいんだよ。ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “What? One aye is enough. I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「らっしゃいらっしゃい、美味しいクレープだよー！」
lines.english: “Fresh crêpes! Get your delicious crêpes right here!”

lines.japanese: 今度のは聞いてすらもらえなかった。
lines.english: This time she didn't even pretend to hear me.

lines.japanese: つか、何その魚屋みたいな呼びこみ。
lines.english: What was with that fishmonger’s sales pitch?
